title: Conditional recursion and transport of slotwise realization shift squares
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ work on the small pro-etale sites with $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ and the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_W$ (module sheaves $M_n$ over $(A_n)_W$ with compatible semilinear transition maps). Use its ordinary unbounded derived category, derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$, total limit $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$, and actual adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ with unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. System operations are inverse image $P_v$ for separated finite-type maps $v$, direct image $S_p$ for proper $p$, quasi-compact open extension $J_j$, and derived tensor, with the integral counterparts of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Restrict input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs are derived complete and constructible. Use the fixed slotwise cochain shifts of [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data], with the signed second tensor slot, and the K-injective strict-tower Roos model for total limit. Write $\chi_H:H(M[r])\to H(M)[r]$ for a designated slot, holding other slots fixed. Let $V$ range over finite well-typed expressions with independently indexed leaf occurrences [def-pur-integral-expression-occurrences], and let $c_V$ be the specified canonical realization maps. Assume the inverse unit and unary and binary insertion maps $a_A,a_\otimes$ commute naturally with all integer shifts in their slots. Assume the actual identities of [lem-pur-integral-realization-recursion]:
$$c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1},\qquad c_{AV}=A_{\rm int}(c_V)a_A(M),\qquad c_{V\otimes T}=(c_V\widehat\otimes^Lc_T)a_\otimes(M,N),$$
where $M=V(\mathcal RK_i)$ and $N=T(\mathcal RK_i)$, with disjoint occurrence sets at each tensor node. Then, for every leaf $i$ and integer $r$,
$$\chi_{V_{\rm int}}c_{V^{(i,r)}}=c_V[r]\,\chi_{\mathcal LV\mathcal R},$$
naturally in the entire input family; the expression's admissible domain is stable under replacing that one leaf by its shift, translating the common finite bounds. Moreover, let a collection of specified system generators $\tau:V\to T$ commute with these slot shifts, and let their corresponding integral maps satisfy the actual intertwining equality $\tau_{\rm int}=c_T\mathcal L(\tau)c_V^{-1}$. Every finite composition and unary or binary expression context of these synchronized generators [def-pur-synchronized-canonical-maps] has both its system and integral shift squares, with the same realization intertwining equality. Tensor contexts retain the side of the designated occurrence, and several independent input changes factor as single-slot changes. This conclusion is conditional on the stated local insertion and generator squares; it asserts none of them.

proof.text: Induct on the ordered finite list, generalizing the admissible input family. The empty case is identity. For a cons update apply the single-leaf square, then the tail induction at that updated family. Map the single square by the remaining output shifts and compose with the tail square. Functor.map_comp and associativity yield exactly the defined treeSourceShifts and treeIntegralShifts. This argument works even for repeated labels, hence in particular under the retained Nodup premise.
